name: Adaiah
overview: Adaiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah known specifically as the son of Joiarib. His identity is primarily recorded in Nehemiah 11:5, which situates him within the post-exilic community of Judah. Beyond his paternal link, no further personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Adaiah means 'adornment of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew meaning that highlights a connection to the Lord. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:5, was not explicitly given by God but carries a devotional significance consistent with biblical naming conventions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Adaiah as the son of Joiarib and infers Hazaiah as his father, establishing a direct paternal lineage. No additional family relationships beyond these are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Adaiah's significance lies in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah during the period described in Nehemiah. His mention as the son of Joiarib connects him to a priestly or Levitical family line, underscoring the restoration and reorganization of the community after the exile. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion in the genealogical record affirms the continuity of God's people and the faithfulness of those who returned to Jerusalem.
